byHand states 1.06^8 ≈ 1.594 and 1.06^9 ≈ 1.689 with no way to reach them on paper, and the 2023 rationale cites x ≈ 8.77, a number only the Desmos route produces. Reachable without Desmos by repeated squaring (or a four-function calculator), so not blocking; show the squaring and tie distractors to hand steps.

fix.old: Need 1.06^n > 4000/2400 = 5/3 ≈ 1.667. 1.06^8 ≈ 1.594 (too small), 1.06^9 ≈ 1.689, so n = 9 and the year is 2024. Distractors: 2023 reads the 8.77 as 8 years, 2025 adds a year after rounding up, 2027 assumes linear growth of 144 per year.
fix.new: Need 1.06^n > 4000/2400 = 5/3 ≈ 1.667. Square repeatedly: 1.06^2 = 1.1236, 1.06^4 = 1.1236^2 ≈ 1.2625, 1.06^8 ≈ 1.2625^2 ≈ 1.594 (too small), and 1.06^9 ≈ 1.594 · 1.06 ≈ 1.689 (large enough). So n = 9 and the year is 2015 + 9 = 2024. Distractors: 2023 stops at n = 8, the last year the population is still below 4,000; 2025 counts 2015 as year 1, adding an extra year; 2027 assumes linear growth of 6% of 2,400, or 144 per year (1,600/144 ≈ 11.1, so 12 years).
